decision: First container remediation experiment for the CRA2 owner-only Cloud Run deployment
decision_limits: No head-to-head validated candidate image results exist. The registry same-digest check is not comparative evidence between Debian remediation and Wolfi. Do not claim a preferred release base.

evidence.claim: Current complete image builds, verifies its runtime smoke, and is blocked on 104 High, Critical or Unknown scan matches; known-vulnerable control passed.

The bound local release scan attributes all 104 blocking matches to 20 Debian binary packages, covering 40 distinct advisory IDs. The scanner reports zero fixed-version entries for those matches. That is not a vendor-level applicability or available-patch determination.

A direct registry read on 2026-11-16 returned the same Linux amd64 debug and nonroot digests as the current builder and runtime pins for those tags. This compares the pinned and current Debian image inputs only, not the two remediation options.
Debian provides official package/advisory status and Distroless tracks Debian updates. Vendor reconciliation can be performed before building a candidate.
Wolfi publishes a package repository for production images. No app-specific Wolfi digest, signature, package resolution or scan was measured here.

flip_conditions: If Debian vendor reconciliation produces no supported path to a clean image, build a digest-pinned Wolfi comparison candidate.
If a verified Wolfi candidate clears the same scan and passes runtime tests while the Debian candidate remains blocked, revisit the release image choice.
If one candidate breaks locked Python/ONNX dependencies, encoder parity, or the cloud entrypoint, it fails the acceptance conditions.

Repository operating directives require a digest-pinned hardened base (Distroless or Wolfi), Syft SBOM and Grype CI, signed artifacts and SLSA build provenance.
Preserve the existing scanner gate and application behavior during base remediation. Judge the first investigation, not image or deployment readiness.
Whether the 40 unique advisory IDs apply to the exact Debian package builds, whether supported fixes are available, or whether a signed Wolfi app image clears the same gate.

smallest_separating_test: Reconcile the 40 advisory IDs against exact Debian source-package versions. For any viable patched Debian image and a signed Wolfi candidate, compare the same locked app on Linux amd64 with fresh Syft and the same Grype database/policy, then boot the cloud entrypoint and run offline smoke. A clean image and a passing detection control are required.
